method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media vocabulary, the advantages and disadvantages of being online, and two key grammar structures: relative pronouns que/quien and modal verbs poder/deber.

SpanishEnglish
las redes socialessocial media
el móvil / el smartphonemobile phone / smartphone
compartirto share
publicarto post / publish
seguir a alguiento follow someone
el seguidor / la seguidorafollower (m/f)
el tiempo de pantallascreen time
puede ser adictivoit can be addictive
mantenerse en contactoto stay in touch
el ciberacosocyberbullying (Higher)
aunquealthough
por un lado… por otro ladoon one hand… on the other hand
debería(mos)I/we should
se puede + infinitiveyou can / one can

Grammar focus 1 — relative pronouns: Use que for things and people ('that/which/who'): una aplicación que uso todos los días (an app that I use every day). Use quien/quienes for people after a preposition: la persona con quien hablo (the person I talk to / with whom I talk). Note: que is never replaced by quien when it is the direct object connector — use que for 'the person that I see' (la persona que veo).

Grammar focus 2 — modal verbs: poder (can/be able to) + infinitive and deber (should/must) + infinitive. In Spanish, the subject pronoun is normally omitted: debes reducir (you should reduce), podemos compartir (we can share). Conditional debería(mos) is softer: deberíamos limitar (we should limit).

Model paragraph: Uso las redes sociales todos los días. Aunque son útiles para mantenerse en contacto con amigos, pueden ser adictivas. Creo que deberíamos limitar nuestro tiempo de pantalla para que no afecte nuestros estudios. (I use social media every day. Although they are useful for staying in touch with friends, they can be addictive. I think we should limit our screen time so that it does not affect our studies.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for social media and online activities
Master the relative pronouns que (things/people) and quien (people after preposition)
Practise modal verbs: poder + infinitive and deber/debería + infinitive
Build balanced arguments using aunque, por un lado… por otro lado

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — social media and technology appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Uso las redes sociales todos los días para compartir fotos y chatear con mis amigos.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Uso las redes sociales = I use social media. todos los días = every day.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: para compartir fotos = to share photos (para + infinitive = in order to). chatear con mis amigos = chat with my friends.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I use social media every day to share photos and chat with my friends.

worked_examples.question: Write a balanced argument about social media using aunque.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Start with the concession (the positive): Aunque las redes sociales son útiles para mantenerse en contacto...

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Add the counter-argument: ...pueden ser adictivas y afectar la salud mental.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Aunque las redes sociales son útiles para mantenerse en contacto, pueden ser adictivas y afectar la salud mental.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish social media vocabulary to its English meaning
Match the Spanish vocabulary to its English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: Las redes sociales son útiles para

gaps.correct_explain: mantenerse en contacto is a fixed phrase meaning 'to stay in touch'. The reflexive form is required.

wrong.mantener: mantener alone is not reflexive. The correct phrase is mantenerse en contacto.

gaps.correct_explain: amigos means friends. Staying in touch with friends is a key advantage of social media.

wrong.enemigos: enemigos means enemies — not what you would stay in touch with!

gaps.correct_explain: sigo is the irregular yo form of seguir (to follow). The stem changes: e → i.

wrong.seguo: seguo is not a valid Spanish form. Seguir is irregular: yo sigo.
wrong.sigue: sigue is the él/ella form. First person singular = sigo.

wrong.sociables: sociables means sociable (adjective for people). The correct adjective in this phrase is sociales.

silver.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: pasaba is the imperfect of pasar. 'I was spending' (ongoing/habitual habit last year) uses the imperfect tense.

wrong.pasé: pasé is the preterite. 'Was spending' (ongoing action) implies the imperfect: pasaba.
wrong.paso: paso is the present tense. El año pasado shows this is past → imperfect: pasaba.

gaps.correct_explain: afectó is the preterite of afectar. The impact on studies was a completed, single result — so preterite is correct.

wrong.afecta: afecta is the present tense. The sentence is about last year → preterite: afectó.

silver.english: Last year I **was spending** too much time online and it **affected** my studies.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Nunca seguo a famosos en las redes sociales.
silver.explanation: Seguir is irregular in the yo form. The stem changes from e to i and the spelling changes: sigo, not seguo. This is a common exam trap.
silver.translation: I never follow celebrities on social media.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: Although social media is useful, it can be addictive.

distractor_labels.es: wrong number — las redes sociales is plural, so use son (plural), not es (singular)

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: In the future I will try to spend less time on my phone.

distractor_labels.su: wrong possessive — 'my' is mi, not su (his/her/your formal)
distractor_labels.más: wrong meaning — 'less' is menos, not más (more)
distractor_labels.intento: wrong tense — 'I will try' is the simple future (intentaré), not the present (intento)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are in a town in Spain and you bump into a Spanish friend. You have a conversation about social media and how you use your phone.

bullets.prompt: Say how you use social media and how much time you spend online each day.
bullets.model_answer: Uso las redes sociales todos los días. Normalmente paso una hora en mi móvil publicando fotos y chateando con amigos.
bullets.note: present tense + time expression + gerunds (publicando, chateando)

bullets.prompt: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of social media.
bullets.model_answer: Por un lado, es una buena manera de mantenerse en contacto. Por otro lado, puede ser adictivo y el ciberacoso es un problema grave.
bullets.note: por un lado / por otro lado structure + puede ser adictivo (note: adictivo agrees with masculine implied subject)

bullets.prompt: Say what happened last year because of your phone use.
bullets.model_answer: El año pasado pasaba demasiado tiempo en línea y afectó mis estudios.
bullets.note: pasaba (imperfect — ongoing habit) + afectó (preterite — completed result)

bullets.prompt: Say what you will do in the future to reduce your screen time.
bullets.model_answer: En el futuro intentaré reducir mi tiempo de pantalla. Creo que deberíamos pasar más tiempo al aire libre.
bullets.note: future intentaré + conditional deberíamos + al aire libre (in the open air)

sentence_parts: el tiempo de pantalla de sus hijos para que no

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive — after me gustaría que
gaps.correct_explain: controlaran is the imperfect subjunctive of controlar. After me gustaría que (I would like it if), Spanish requires the imperfect subjunctive.

wrong.controlan: controlan is the present indicative. After me gustaría que, use the imperfect subjunctive: controlaran.
wrong.controlen: controlen is the present subjunctive. After me gustaría que, the imperfect subjunctive is preferred: controlaran.

gaps.rule: Present or imperfect subjunctive — after para que
gaps.correct_explain: pasen (present subjunctive) or pasaran (imperfect subjunctive) are both acceptable after para que (so that).

wrong.pasan: pasan is the present indicative. After para que, the subjunctive is required: pasen.

gold.english: I would like parents to **control** their children's screen time so that they **don't spend** too much time online.
